increase  in  the  mass  of  capital  depends  on  its  existing  magnitude.

text: But, on the other hand, if this magnitude is given, the proportion of its growth, i.e., the rate of its increment, depends on the rate of profit.
text_raw:
But,  on  the  other  hand,  if  this  magnitude  is  given,  the  proportion
of  its  growth,  i.e.,  the  rate  of  its  increment,  depends  on  the  rate  of
profit.

text: The increase in the productiveness (which, moreover, we repeat, always goes hand in hand with a depreciation of the available capital) can directly only increase the value of the existing capita! if by raising the rate of profit it increases that portion of the value of the annual product which is reconverted into capital.
text_raw:
The  increase  in  the  productiveness  (which,  moreover,  we
repeat,  always  goes  hand  in  hand  with  a  depreciation  of  the
available  capital)  can  directly  only  increase  the  value  of  the
existing  capita!  if  by  raising  the  rate  of  profit  it  increases  that
portion  of  the  value  of  the  annual  product  which  is  reconverted
into  capital.

text: As concerns the productivity of labour, this can only occur (since this productivity has nothing direct to do with the value of the existing capital) by raising the relative surplus- value, or reducing the value of the constant capital, so that the commodities which enter either the reproduction of labour-power, or the elements of constant capital, are cheapened.
text_raw:
As  concerns  the  productivity  of  labour,  this  can
only  occur  (since  this  productivity  has  nothing  direct  to  do  with
the  value  of  the  existing  capital)  by  raising  the  relative  surplus-
value,  or  reducing  the  value  of  the  constant  capital,  so  that  the
commodities  which  enter  either  the  reproduction  of  labour-power,
or  the  elements  of  constant  capital,  are  cheapened.

text: Both imply a depreciation of the existing capital, and both go hand in hand with a reduction of the variable capital in relation to the con¬ stant.
text_raw:
Both  imply
a  depreciation  of  the  existing  capital,  and  both  go  hand  in  hand
with  a  reduction  of  the  variable  capital  in  relation  to  the  con¬
stant.

text: Both cause a fall in the rate of profit, and both slow it down.
text_raw: Both  cause  a  fall  in  the  rate  of  profit,  and  both  slow  it  down.

text: Furthermore, inasmuch as an increased rate of profit causes a greater demand for labour, it tends to increase the working population and thus the material, whose exploitation makes real capital out of capital.
text_raw:
Furthermore,  inasmuch  as  an  increased  rate  of  profit  causes  a
greater  demand  for  labour,  it  tends  to  increase  the  working
population  and  thus  the  material,  whose  exploitation  makes  real

text: Indirectly, however, the development of the productivity of la¬ bour contributes to the increase of the value of the existing capital by increasing the mass and variety of use-values in which the same exchange-value is represented' and which form the material sub¬ stance, i.e., the material elements of capital, the material objects making up the constant capital directly, and the variable capital at least indirectly.

Indirectly,  however,  the  development  of  the  productivity  of  la¬
bour  contributes  to  the  increase  of  the  value  of  the  existing  capital

stance,  i.e.,  the  material  elements  of  capital,  the  material  objects
making  up  the  constant  capital  directly,  and  the  variable  capital

text: INTERNAL CONTRADICTIONS OF THE LAW
text_raw: INTERNAL  CONTRADICTIONS  OF  THE  LAW

text: however, are not to be regarded merely as existing side by side in repose, as Ricardo does.

however,  are  not  to  be  regarded  merely  as  existing  side  by  side  in

They  contain  a  contradiction  which
manifests  itself  in  contradictory  tendencies  and  phenomena.

text: These antagonistic agencies counteract each other simultaneously.
text_raw:
These
antagonistic  agencies  counteract  each  other  simultaneously.

text: Alongside the stimulants of an actual increase of the labouring population, which spring from the increase of the portion of the total social product serving as capital, there are agencies which create a merely relative over-population.
text_raw:
Alongside  the  stimulants  of  an  actual  increase  of  the  labouring
population,  which  spring  from  the  increase  of  the  portion  of  the
total  social  product  serving  as  capital,  there  are  agencies  which

text: Alongside the fall in the rate of profit mass of capitals grows, and hand in hand with this there occurs a depreciation of existing capitals which checks the fall and gives an accelerating motion to the accumulation of capital-values.
text_raw:
Alongside  the  fall  in  the  rate  of  profit  mass  of  capitals  grows,
and  hand  in  hand  with  this  there  occurs  a  depreciation  of  existing
capitals  which  checks  the  fall  and  gives  an  accelerating  motion

text: Alongside the development of productivity there develops a higher composition of capital, i.e., the relative decrease of the ratio of variable to constant capital.
text_raw:
Alongside  the  development  of  productivity  there  develops  a
higher  composition  of  capital,  i.e.,  the  relative  decrease  of  the
ratio  of  variable  to  constant  capital.

text: These different influences may at one time operate predomi¬ nantly side by side in space, and at another succeed each other in time.

These  different  influences  may  at  one  time  operate  predomi¬
nantly  side  by  side  in  space,  and  at  another  succeed  each  other
in  time.

text: From time to time the conflict of antagonistic agencies finds vent in crises.
text_raw:
From  time  to  time  the  conflict  of  antagonistic  agencies
finds  vent  in  crises.

text: The crises are always but momentary and forcible solutions of the existing contradictions.
text_raw:
The  crises  are  always  but  momentary
and  forcible  solutions  of  the  existing  contradictions.

text: They are violent eruptions which for a time restore the disturbed equilibrium.
text_raw:
They  are
violent  eruptions  which  for  a  time  restore  the  disturbed
equilibrium.

text: The contradiction, to put it in a very general way, consists in that the capitalist mode of production involves a tendency towards absolute development of the productive forces, regard¬ less of the value and surplus-value it contains, and regardless of the social conditions under which capitalist production takes place; while, on the other hand, its aim is to preserve the value of the existing capital and promote its self-expansion to the highest limit (i.e., to promote an ever more rapid growth of this value).
text_raw:
The  contradiction,  to  put  it  in  a  very  general  way,  consists
in  that  the  capitalist  mode  of  production  involves  a  tendency
towards  absolute  development  of  the  productive  forces,  regard¬
less  of  the  value  and  surplus-value  it  contains,  and  regardless
of  the  social  conditions  under  which  capitalist  production  takes
place;  while,  on  the  other  hand,  its  aim  is  to  preserve  the  value
of  the  existing  capital  and  promote  its  self-expansion  to  the  highest
limit  (i.e.,  to  promote  an  ever  more  rapid  growth  of  this  value).

text: The specific feature about it is that it uses the existing value of capital as a means of increasing this value to the utmost.
text_raw:
The  specific  feature  about  it  is  that  it  uses  the  existing  value  of
capital  as  a  means  of  increasing  this  value  to  the  utmost.

text: The methods by which it accomplishes this include the fall of the rate of profit, depreciation of existing capital, and development of the productive forces of labour at the expense of already created productive forces.
text_raw:
The

text: The confusion is augmented by the attendant collapse of the credit system, which develops simultaneously with capital, and leads to violent and acute crises, to sudden and forcible depreciations, to the actual stagnation and disruption of the process of reproduc¬ tion, and thus to a real falling off in reproduction.

confusion  is  augmented  by  the  attendant  collapse  of  the  credit

text: On the other hand, the fall in prices and the competitive struggle would have driven every capitalist to lower the individual value of his total product below its general value by means of new machines, new and improved working methods, new combinations, i.e., to increase the productivity of a given quantity of labour, to lower the proportion of variable to constant capital, and thereby to release some labourers; in short, to create an artificial over-population.

text: Yet it would still be over-production, because capital would be unable to exploit labour to the degree required by a “sound”, “normal” development of the process of capitalist production, to a degree which would at least increase the mass of profit along with the growing mass of the employed capital; to a degree which would, therefore, prevent the rate of profit from falling as much as the capital grows, or even more rapidly.

Yet  it  would  still  be  over-production,  because  capital  would

text: Over-production of capital is never anything more than over¬ production of means of production— of means of labour and necessities of life — which may serve as capital, i.e., may serve to exploit labour at a given degree of exploitation; a fall in the intensity of exploitation below a certain point, however, calls forth disturbances, and stoppages in the capitalist production

necessities  of  life — which  may  serve  as  capital,  i.e.,  may  serve

text: The circumstances which increased the productiveness of labour, augmented the mass of produced commodities, expanded markets, accelerated accumulation of capital both in terms of its mass and its value, and lowered the rate of profit — these same circumstances have also created, and continuously create, a relative over¬ population, an over-population of labourers not employed by the surplus-capital owing to the low degree of exploitation at which alone they could be employed, or at least owing to the low rate of profit which they would yield at the given degree of exploitation.
text_raw:
The  circumstances
which  increased  the  productiveness  of  labour,  augmented  the
mass  of  produced  commodities,  expanded  markets,  accelerated
accumulation  of  capital  both  in  terms  of  its  mass  and  its  value,
and  lowered  the  rate  of  profit — these  same  circumstances
have  also  created,  and  continuously  create,  a  relative  over¬
population,  an  over-population  of  labourers  not  employed  by
the  surplus-capital  owing  to  the  low  degree  of  exploitation
at  which  alone  they  could  be  employed,  or  at  least  owing  to  the

exploitation.

text: If capital is sent abroad, this is not done because it absolutely could not be applied at home, but because it can be employed at a higher rate of profit in a foreign country.

But  such  capital
is  absolute  excess  capital  for  the  employed  labouring  population

text: It exists as such alongside the relative over-population, and this is an illustration of how both of them exist side by side, and mutually influence one another.

It  exists  as  such  alongside

text: Since the aim of capital is not to minister to certain wants, but to produce profit, and since it accomplishes this purpose by methods which adapt the mass of production to the scale of production, not vice versa, a rift must continually ensue between the limited dimen¬ sions of consumption under capitalism and a production which forever tends to exceed this immanent barrier.
text_raw:
Since  the
aim  of  capital  is  not  to  minister  to  certain  wants,  but  to  produce
profit,  and  since  it  accomplishes  this  purpose  by  methods  which
adapt  the  mass  of  production  to  the  scale  of  production,  not  vice
versa,  a  rift  must  continually  ensue  between  the  limited  dimen¬
sions  of  consumption  under  capitalism  and  a  production  which
forever  tends  to  exceed  this  immanent  barrier.

Furthermore,

If  it  is  finally  said  that  the  capitalists  have  only

text: In short, all these objections to the obvious phenomena of over-production (phenomena which pay no heed to these objections) amount to the contention that the barriers of capitalist production are not barriers of production generally, and therefore not barriers of this specific, capitalist mode of production.

all  these  objections  to  the  obvious  phenomena  of  over-production

the  contention  that  the  barriers  of  capitalist  production  are  not
barriers  of  production  generally,  and  therefore  not  barriers  of  this
specific,  capitalist  mode  of  production.

text: The contradiction of the capitalist mode of production, however, lies precisely in its tendency towards an absolute development of the productive forces, which continually come into conflict with the specific conditions of production in which capital moves, and alone can move.

The  contradiction  of  the

text: 1) In that the development of the productivity of labour creates out of the falling rate of profit a law which at a certain point comes into antagonistic conflict with this development and must be overcome constantly through crises.

opposite  directions,  it  follows  that  the  mass  of  average  profit

most  advanced  branches  of  industry.

chapter_title: Book  II.*  To  take  the  total  capital  of  society,  one  part  of  it —
text: We have seen that the existence of capital as commodity- capital and the metamorphosis it undergoes within the sphere of circulation in the market as commodity-capital — a metamorpho¬ sis which resolves itself into buying and selling, converting commodity-capital into money-capital and money-capital into com¬ modity-capital — that this forms a phase in the reproduction process of industrial capital, hence in its process of production as a whole.
text_raw:
We  have  seen  that  the  existence  of  capital  as  commodity-
capital  and  the  metamorphosis  it  undergoes  within  the  sphere  of
circulation  in  the  market  as  commodity-capital — a  metamorpho¬
sis  which  resolves  itself  into  buying  and  selling,  converting
commodity-capital  into  money-capital  and  money-capital  into  com¬
modity-capital — that  this  forms  a  phase  in  the  reproduction
process  of  industrial  capital,  hence  in  its  process  of  production
as  a  whole.

chapter_title: Book  II.*  To  take  the  total  capital  of  society,  one  part  of  it —

chapter_title: Book  II.*  To  take  the  total  capital  of  society,  one  part  of  it —
text: One portion of the total social capital is continually on the market in the form of capital of circulation, passing through this process of transmutation, although for each individual capital its existence as commodity- capital, and its metamorphosis as such, merely represent ever- vanishing and ever renewed nodal points— i.e., stages of transi¬ tion in the continuity of its production process, and although the elements of commodity-capital in the market vary continuously for this reason, being constantly withdrawn from the commodity- market and equally periodically returned to it as new products of the process of production.
text_raw:
One  portion  of  the  total  social
capital  is  continually  on  the  market  in  the  form  of  capital  of
circulation,  passing  through  this  process  of  transmutation,
although  for  each  individual  capital  its  existence  as  commodity-
capital,  and  its  metamorphosis  as  such,  merely  represent  ever-
vanishing  and  ever  renewed  nodal  points— i.e.,  stages  of  transi¬
tion  in  the  continuity  of  its  production  process,  and  although  the
elements  of  commodity-capital  in  the  market  vary  continuously
for  this  reason,  being  constantly  withdrawn  from  the  commodity-
market  and  equally  periodically  returned  to  it  as  new  products
of  the  process  of  production.

text: We have seen- in Book II* that the pure functions of capital in the sphere of circulation — the operations which the industrial capitalist must perform, first, to realise the value of his com¬ modities, and second, to reconvert this value into elements of production, operations effecting the metamorphosis of commodity- capital, C' — M— C, hence the acts of selling and buying — produce neither value nor surplus-value.
text_raw:
We  have  seen-  in  Book  II*  that  the  pure  functions  of  capital
in  the  sphere  of  circulation — the  operations  which  the  industrial
capitalist  must  perform,  first,  to  realise  the  value  of  his  com¬
modities,  and  second,  to  reconvert  this  value  into  elements  of
production,  operations  effecting  the  metamorphosis  of  commodity-
capital,  C' — M— C,  hence  the  acts  of  selling  and  buying — produce
neither  value  nor  surplus-value.

text: It was rather seen that the time required for this purpose, objectively in regard to commodities and subjectively in regard to the capitalist, sets the limit to the pro¬ duction of value and surplus-value.
text_raw:
It  was  rather  seen  that  the  time
required  for  this  purpose,  objectively  in  regard  to  commodities  and
subjectively  in  regard  to  the  capitalist,  sets  the  limit  to  the  pro¬
duction  of  value  and  surplus-value.

text: What is true of the metamor¬ phosis of commodity-capital in general, is, of course, not in the least altered by the fact that a part of it may assume the shape of commercial capital, or that the operations, effecting the metamor¬ phosis of commodity-capital, appear as the special concern of a special group of capitalists, or as the exclusive function of a portion of the money-capital.
text_raw:
What  is  true  of  the  metamor¬
phosis  of  commodity-capital  in  general,  is,  of  course,  not  in  the
least  altered  by  the  fact  that  a  part  of  it  may  assume  the  shape  of
commercial  capital,  or  that  the  operations,  effecting  the  metamor¬
phosis  of  commodity-capital,  appear  as  the  special  concern  of  a
special  group  of  capitalists,  or  as  the  exclusive  function  of  a
portion  of  the  money-capital.

text: If selling and buying commodities — and that is what the metamorphosis of commodity-capital C'— M — C amounts to — by industrial capitalists themselves are not operations which create value or surplus-value, they will certainly not create either of these when carried out by persons other than the industrial capitalists.
text_raw:
If  selling  and  buying  commodities  —
and  that  is  what  the  metamorphosis  of  commodity-capital
C'— M — C  amounts  to — by  industrial  capitalists  themselves  are  not
operations  which  create  value  or  surplus-value,  they  will  certainly
not  create  either  of  these  when  carried  out  by  persons  other  than
the  industrial  capitalists.

text: Furthermore, if that portion of the total social capital, which must continually be on hand as money- capital, in order that the process of reproduction is not interrupt¬ ed by the process of circulation and proceeds continuously — if this money-capital creates neither value nor surplus-value, it cannot acquire the properties of creating them by being continu¬ ally thrown into circulation by some section of capitalists other than the industrial capitalists, to perform the same function.
text_raw:
Furthermore,  if  that  portion  of  the
total  social  capital,  which  must  continually  be  on  hand  as  money-
capital,  in  order  that  the  process  of  reproduction  is  not  interrupt¬

ally  thrown  into  circulation  by  some  section  of  capitalists  other

text: Commercial capital, therefore — stripped of all heterogeneous functions, such as storing, expressing, transporting, distributing, retailing, which may be connected with it, and confined to its true function of buying in order to sell — creates neither value nor surplus-value, but acts as middleman in their realisation and thereby simultaneously in the actual exchange of commodities, i.e., in their transfer from hand to hand, in the social metabolism.
text_raw:
Commercial  capital,  therefore — stripped  of  all  heterogeneous
functions,  such  as  storing,  expressing,  transporting,  distributing,
retailing,  which  may  be  connected  with  it,  and  confined  to  its
true  function  of  buying  in  order  to  sell — creates  neither  value  nor
surplus-value,  but  acts  as  middleman  in  their  realisation  and
thereby  simultaneously  in  the  actual  exchange  of  commodities,  i.e.,
in  their  transfer  from  hand  to  hand,  in  the  social  metabolism.

text: Nevertheless, since the circulation phase of industrial capital is just as much a phase of the reproduction process as production is, the capital operating independently in the process of circulation must yield the average annual profit just as well as capital operating in the various branches of production.
text_raw:
Nevertheless,  since  the  circulation  phase  of  industrial  capital  is  just
as  much  a  phase  of  the  reproduction  process  as  production  is,  the
capital  operating  independently  in  the  process  of  circulation  must
yield  the  average  annual  profit  just  as  well  as  capital  operating  in
the  various  branches  of  production.

text: Since merchant’s capital does not itself produce surplus-value, it is evident that the surplus-value which it pockets in the form of average profit must be a portion of the surplus-value produced by the total productive capital.

text: It is plain that the merchant can draw his profit only out of the price of the commodities he sells, and plainer still that the profit he makes in selling his commodities must be equal to the difference between his purchase price and his selling price, i.e., equal to the excess of the latter over the former.

between  his  purchase  price  and  his  selling  price,  i.e.,  equal
to  the  excess  of  the  latter  over  the  former.

text: Just as industrial capital realises only such profits as already exist in the value of commodities as surplus-value, so merchant’s capital realises profits only because the entire surplus-value, or profit, has not as yet been fully realised in the price charged for the commodities by the industrial capitalist.39 The merchant’s selling price thus exceeds the purchase price not because the former exceeds the total value, but because the latter is below this value.

value,  but  because  the  latter  is  below  this  value.

capitalist,  whose  direct  agent  he  is,  while  his  employer  pockets
both  the  industrial  and  the  commercial  profit.

text: But in all these cases, although his income may appear to the circulation agent as an ordinary wage, as payment for work performed, and although, where it does not so appear, the profit may be no larger than the wage of a better-paid labourer, his income is derived solely from the mercantile profit.

text: 2) a longer stay of his product in money- or commodity-form, in the circulation process, hence in a process where it does not expand value and where the direct production process is interrupted.
text_raw:
2)  a  longer  stay  of  his  product  in  money-  or
commodity-form,  in  the  circulation  process,  hence  in  a  process
where  it  does  not  expand  value  and  where  the  direct  production

text: If this process is not to be interrupted, production must either be curtailed, or more money-capital must be advanced to maintain the process of production on the same scale.
text_raw:
If  this  process  is  not  to  be  interrupted,
production  must  either  be  curtailed,  or  more  money-capital
must  be  advanced  to  maintain  the  process  of  production  on  the

text: This means that each time either a smaller profit is made on the capital hitherto invested, or that additional money-capital must be advanced to make the previous profit.

This  means  that  each  time  either  a  smaller  profit
is  made  on  the  capital  hitherto  invested,  or  that  additional
money-capital  must  be  advanced  to  make  the  previous  profit.

text: All this remains unchanged when the merchant takes the place of the industrial capitalist.
text_raw:
All  this  remains  unchanged  when  the  merchant  takes  the  place
of  the  industrial  capitalist.

text: Instead of the industrial capitalist devoting more time to the process of circulation, it is the mer¬ chant who is so engaged; instead of the industrial capitalist it is the merchant who advances additional capital for circulation; or, what amounts to the same thing, instead of a large portion of the industrial capital being continually diverted into the process of circulation, it is the merchant’s capital which is wholly tied up in it; and instead of making a smaller profit, the industrial capitalist must yield a portion of his profit wholly to the merchant.
text_raw:
Instead  of  the  industrial  capitalist
devoting  more  time  to  the  process  of  circulation,  it  is  the  mer¬
chant  who  is  so  engaged;  instead  of  the  industrial  capitalist  it
is  the  merchant  who  advances  additional  capital  for  circulation;
or,  what  amounts  to  the  same  thing,  instead  of  a  large  portion
of  the  industrial  capital  being  continually  diverted  into  the
process  of  circulation,  it  is  the  merchant’s  capital  which  is
wholly  tied  up  in  it;  and  instead  of  making  a  smaller  profit,
the  industrial  capitalist  must  yield  a  portion  of  his  profit  wholly
to  the  merchant.

text: So long as merchant’s capital remains within the bounds in which it is necessary, the only difference is that this division of the functions of capital reduces the time exclu¬ sively used up in the process of circulation, that less additional capital is advanced for this purpose, and that the loss in total profit, represented by mercantile profit, is smaller than it would otherwise have been.
text_raw:
So  long  as  merchant’s  capital  remains  within

text: In so far as these additional costs connected with the business of circulation are transferred from the industrial to the commer¬ cial capitalist, there takes place a similar reduction in the rate of profit, but to a lesser degree and in a different way.

cial  capitalist,  there  takes  place  a  similar  reduction  in  the  rate

text: It now develops that the merchant advances more capital than would be necessary if these costs did not exist, and that the profit on this additional capital increases the amount of the commercial profit, so that more of the merchant’s capital joins industrial capital in levelling the average rate of profit and thereby the average profit falls.

text: What about the commercial wage¬ workers employed by the commercial capitalist, here the merchant?

What  about  the  commercial  wage¬
workers  employed  by  the  commercial  capitalist,  here  the  merchant?

text: In one respect, such a commercial employee is a wage-worker like any other.
text_raw:
In  one  respect,  such  a  commercial  employee  is  a  wage-worker
like  any  other.

text: In the first place, his labour-power is bought with the variable capital of the merchant, not with money expended as revenue, and consequently it is not bought for private service, but for the purpose of expanding the value of the capital advanced for it.
text_raw:
In  the  first  place,  his  labour-power  is  bought  with
the  variable  capital  of  the  merchant,  not  with  money  expended
as  revenue,  and  consequently  it  is  not  bought  for  private  service,
but  for  the  purpose  of  expanding  the  value  of  the  capital  advanced
for  it.

text: In the second place, the value of his labour-power, and thus his wages, are determined as those of other wage-workers, i.e., by the cost of production and reproduction of his specific labour-power, not by the product of his labour.
text_raw:
In  the  second  place,  the  value  of  his  labour-power,  and
thus  his  wages,  are  determined  as  those  of  other  wage-workers,
i.e.,  by  the  cost  of  production  and  reproduction  of  his  specific
labour-power,  not  by  the  product  of  his  labour.

text: COMMERCIAL PROFIT
text_raw: COMMERCIAL  PROFIT

text: However, we must make the same distinction between him and the wage-workers directly employed by industrial capital which exists between industrial capital and merchant's capital, and thus between the industrial capitalist and the merchant.
text_raw:
However,  we  must  make  the  same  distinction  between  him
and  the  wage-workers  directly  employed  by  industrial  capital
which  exists  between  industrial  capital  and  merchant's  capital,
and  thus  between  the  industrial  capitalist  and  the  merchant.

text: Since the merchant, as a mere agent of circulation, produces neither value nor surplus-value (for the additional value which he adds to the commodities through his expenses resolves itself into an addition of previously existing values, although the question here poses itself, how he preserves this value of his constant capital?) it follows that the mercantile workers em¬ ployed by him in these same functions cannot directly create surplus-value for him.
text_raw:
Since  the  merchant,  as  a  mere  agent  of  circulation,  produces
neither  value  nor  surplus-value  (for  the  additional  value  which
he  adds  to  the  commodities  through  his  expenses  resolves  itself
into  an  addition  of  previously  existing  values,  although  the
question  here  poses  itself,  how  he  preserves  this  value  of  his
constant  capital?)  it  follows  that  the  mercantile  workers  em¬
ployed  by  him  in  these  same  functions  cannot  directly  create
surplus-value  for  him.

text: Here, as in the case of productive labourers, we assume that wages are determined by the value of the labour- power, and that, hence, the merchant does not enrich himself by depressing wages, so that he does not enter into his cost account an advance for labour which he has paid only in part; in other words, that he does not enrich himself through cheating his clerks, etc.
text_raw:
Here,  as  in  the  case  of  productive  labourers,
we  assume  that  wages  are  determined  by  the  value  of  the  labour-
power,  and  that,  hence,  the  merchant  does  not  enrich  himself
by  depressing  wages,  so  that  he  does  not  enter  into  his  cost  account
an  advance  for  labour  which  he  has  paid  only  in  part;  in  other
words,  that  he  does  not  enrich  himself  through  cheating  his
clerks,  etc.

text: The difficulty as concerns mercantile wage-workers is by no means to explain how they produce direct profits for their em¬ ployer without creating any direct surplus-value (of which profit is but a transmuted form).
text_raw:
The  difficulty  as  concerns  mercantile  wage-workers  is  by  no
means  to  explain  how  they  produce  direct  profits  for  their  em¬
ployer  without  creating  any  direct  surplus-value  (of  which  profit
is  but  a  transmuted  form).

text: This question has, indeed, already been solved in the general analysis of commercial profits.
text_raw:
This  question  has,  indeed,  already
been  solved  in  the  general  analysis  of  commercial  profits.

text: Just as industrial capital makes profit by selling labour embodied and realised in commodities, for which it has not paid any equiv¬ alent, so merchant’s capital derives profit from not paying in full to productive capital for all the unpaid labour contained in the commodities (in commodities, in so far as capital invested in their production functions as an aliquot part of the total industrial capital), and by demanding payment for this unpaid portion still contained in the commodities when making a sale.
text_raw:
Just
as  industrial  capital  makes  profit  by  selling  labour  embodied
and  realised  in  commodities,  for  which  it  has  not  paid  any  equiv¬
alent,  so  merchant’s  capital  derives  profit  from  not  paying
in  full  to  productive  capital  for  all  the  unpaid  labour  contained
in  the  commodities  (in  commodities,  in  so  far  as  capital  invested
in  their  production  functions  as  an  aliquot  part  of  the  total
industrial  capital),  and  by  demanding  payment  for  this  unpaid
portion  still  contained  in  the  commodities  when  making  a  sale.

text: The relation of merchant’s capital to surplus-value is different from that of industrial capital.
text_raw:
The  relation  of  merchant’s  capital  to  surplus-value  is  different
from  that  of  industrial  capital.

text: The latter produces surplus- value by directly appropriating the unpaid labour of others.
text_raw:
The  latter  produces  surplus-
value  by  directly  appropriating  the  unpaid  labour  of  others.

text: The former appropriates a portion of this surplus-value by having this portion transferred from industrial capital to itself.
text_raw:
The  former  appropriates  a  portion  of  this  surplus-value  by  having
this  portion  transferred  from  industrial  capital  to  itself.

text: It is only through its function of realising values that mer¬ chant’s capital acts as capital in the process of reproduction, and hence draws on the surplus-value produced by the total capital.
text_raw:
It  is  only  through  its  function  of  realising  values  that  mer¬
chant’s  capital  acts  as  capital  in  the  process  of  reproduction,
and  hence  draws  on  the  surplus-value  produced  by  the  total
capital.

text: The mass of the individual merchant’s profits depends on the mass of capital that he can apply in this process, and he can apply so much more of it in buying and selling, the more the unpaid labour of his clerks.

The  mass  of  the  individual  merchant’s  profits  depends
on  the  mass  of  capital  that  he  can  apply  in  this  process,  and  he
can  apply  so  much  more  of  it  in  buying  and  selling,  the  more
the  unpaid  labour  of  his  clerks.

text: (We must therefore analyse the following points: the mer¬ chant’s variable capital; the law of necessary labour in the sphere of circulation; how the merchant’s labour maintains the value of his constant capital; the part played by merchant’s capital in the process of reproduction as a whole; and, finally, the dupli¬ cation in commodity-capital and money-capital, on the one hand, and in commercial capital and money-dealing capital on the other.)

division  of  labour  in  a  commercial  office,  in  which  one  keeps

text: The number of turnovers of a given merchant’s capital, there¬ fore, is analogous in this case to the repeated cycles of money as a mere medium of circulation.
text_raw:
The  number  of  turnovers  of  a  given  merchant’s  capital,  there¬
fore,  is  analogous  in  this  case  to  the  repeated  cycles  of  money  as
a  mere  medium  of  circulation.

text: Just as the same thaler buys ten times its value in commodities in making ten cycles, so the same money-capital of the merchant, when turned over ten times, buys ten times its value in commodities, or realises a total commodity-capital of ten times its value; a merchant’s capital of 100, for instance, a ten-fold value = 1,000.

Just  as  the  same  thaler  buys  ten
times  its  value  in  commodities  in  making  ten  cycles,  so  the  same

text: But there is this differ¬ ence:

ence:

text: In the cycle of money as a medium of circulation it is the same piece of money that passes through different hands, thus repeatedly performing the same function and hence making up for the mass of the circulating pieces of money by its velocity.
text_raw:
In  the  cycle  of  money  as  a  medium  of  circulation  it  is  the
same  piece  of  money  that  passes  through  different  hands,  thus
repeatedly  performing  the  same  function  and  hence  making  up
for  the  mass  of  the  circulating  pieces  of  money  by  its  velocity.

text: But in the merchant’s case it is the same money capital, the same money-value, regardless of what pieces of money it may be composed, which repeatedly buys and sells commodity-capital to the amount of its value and which therefore returns to the same hands, the same point of departure as M + AM, i.e., value plus surplus-value.
text_raw:
But  in  the  merchant’s  case  it  is  the  same  money  capital,  the  same
money-value,  regardless  of  what  pieces  of  money  it  may  be
composed,  which  repeatedly  buys  and  sells  commodity-capital  to

hands,  the  same  point  of  departure  as  M  +  AM,  i.e.,  value  plus
surplus-value.

text: This characterises its turnover as a capital turn¬ over.

over.

text: A repeated turnover of commercial capital, however, never connotes more than repeated buying and selling; while a repeat¬ ed turnover of industrial capital connotes the periodicity and renovation of the entire reproduction process (which includes the process of consumption).

text: While, therefore, a closer inspection of the influence of the period of turnover on the formation of values by industrial capi¬ tal leads us back to the general law and to the basis of political economy, that the values of commodities are determined by the labour-time contained in them, the influence of the turnovers of merchant’s capital on mercantile prices reveals phenomena which, without benefit of a very far-reaching analysis of the con¬ necting links, seem to point to a purely arbitrary determination of prices; namely, that they are fixed by a capital simply bent upon pocketing a certain quantity of profit in a year.

text: MONEY- DEALING CAPITAL
text_raw: MONEY- DEALING  CAPITAL

text: The purely technical movements performed by money in the circulation process of industrial, and, as we may now add, of commercial capital (since it takes over a part of the circulation movement of industrial capital as its own, peculiar movement), if individualised as a function of some particular capital per¬ forming just these, and only these, operations as its specific oper¬ ations, convert this capital into money-dealing capital.
text_raw:
The  purely  technical  movements  performed  by  money  in  the
circulation  process  of  industrial,  and,  as  we  may  now  add,  of
commercial  capital  (since  it  takes  over  a  part  of  the  circulation
movement  of  industrial  capital  as  its  own,  peculiar  movement),
if  individualised  as  a  function  of  some  particular  capital  per¬
forming  just  these,  and  only  these,  operations  as  its  specific  oper¬
ations,  convert  this  capital  into  money-dealing  capital.

text: A portion of industrial capital, and, more precisely, also of commercial cap¬ ital, not only obtains all the time in the form of money, as money- capital in general, but as money-capital engaged precisely in these technical functions.
text_raw:
A  portion
of  industrial  capital,  and,  more  precisely,  also  of  commercial  cap¬
ital,  not  only  obtains  all  the  time  in  the  form  of  money,  as  money-
capital  in  general,  but  as  money-capital  engaged  precisely  in
these  technical  functions.

text: A definite part of the total capital dissociates itself from the rest and stands apart in the form of money-capital, whose capitalist function consists exclusively in performing these operations for the entire class of industrial and commercial capitalists.
text_raw:
A  definite  part  of  the  total  capital
dissociates  itself  from  the  rest  and  stands  apart  in  the  form  of
money-capital,  whose  capitalist  function  consists  exclusively  in
performing  these  operations  for  the  entire  class  of  industrial  and
commercial  capitalists.

text: As in the case of commercial capital, a portion of industrial capital engaged in the circulation process in the form of money-capital separates from the rest and per¬ forms these operations of the reproduction process for all the other capital.
text_raw:
As  in  the  case  of  commercial  capital,
a  portion  of  industrial  capital  engaged  in  the  circulation  process
in  the  form  of  money-capital  separates  from  the  rest  and  per¬
forms  these  operations  of  the  reproduction  process  for  all  the
other  capital.

text: The movements of this money-capital are, therefore, once more merely movements of an individualised part of in¬ dustrial capital engaged in the reproduction process.
text_raw:
The  movements  of  this  money-capital  are,  therefore,
once  more  merely  movements  of  an  individualised  part  of  in¬
dustrial  capital  engaged  in  the  reproduction  process.

text: It is only when, and in so far as, capital is newly invested — which also applies to accumulation — that capital in money-form appears as the starting-point and the end result of the movement.
text_raw:
It  is  only  when,  and  in  so  far  as,  capital  is  newly  invested —
which  also  applies  to  accumulation — that  capital  in  money-form
appears  as  the  starting-point  and  the  end  result  of  the  movement.

text: But for all capitals already engaged in the process, these first and last points appear merely as points of transit.
text_raw:
But  for  all  capitals  already  engaged  in  the  process,  these  first
and  last  points  appear  merely  as  points  of  transit.

text: Since, as already seen in the case of simple commodity-circulation, from the moment of leaving the sphere of production to the moment
text_raw:
Since,  as
already  seen  in  the  case  of  simple  commodity-circulation,  from
the  moment  of  leaving  the  sphere  of  production  to  the  moment

text: of its re-entry industrial capital undergoes the metamorphosis C' — M — C, M in fact represents the end result of one phase of the metamorphosis, just to become the starting-point of the reverse phase, which supplements it.
text_raw:
of  its  re-entry  industrial  capital  undergoes  the  metamorphosis
C' — M — C,  M  in  fact  represents  the  end  result  of  one  phase  of
the  metamorphosis,  just  to  become  the  starting-point  of  the
reverse  phase,  which  supplements  it.

text: And although the C — M of industrial capital is always M — C — M for merchant’s capital, the actual process for the latter is continually also C— M — C once it has begun to function.
text_raw:
And  although  the  C — M
of  industrial  capital  is  always  M — C — M  for  merchant’s  capital,
the  actual  process  for  the  latter  is  continually  also  C— M — C  once
it  has  begun  to  function.

text: But it performs the acts C — M and M — C simultaneously.
text_raw:
But  it  performs  the  acts  C — M  and
M — C  simultaneously.

text: This is to say that there is not just one capital in the stage C — M while another is in the stage M — C, but that the same capital buys continually and sells continually at one and the same time because of the continuity of the production process.
text_raw:
This  is  to  say  that  there  is  not  just  one
capital  in  the  stage  C — M  while  another  is  in  the  stage  M — C,  but
that  the  same  capital  buys  continually  and  sells  continually  at
one  and  the  same  time  because  of  the  continuity  of  the  production
process.

text: It is to be found always in both stages at one and the same time.
text_raw:
It  is  to  be  found  always  in  both  stages  at  one  and  the  same
time.

text: While one of its parts turns into money, later to be recon¬ verted into commodities, another turns simultaneously into commodities, to be reconverted into money.
text_raw:
While  one  of  its  parts  turns  into  money,  later  to  be  recon¬
verted  into  commodities,  another  turns  simultaneously  into
commodities,  to  be  reconverted  into  money.

text: It all depends on the form of the commodity exchange whether the money serves here as a means of circulation or of payment.
text_raw:
It  all  depends  on  the  form  of  the  commodity  exchange  whether
the  money  serves  here  as  a  means  of  circulation  or  of  payment.

text: In both cases the capitalist has to pay out money constantly to many persons, and to receive money continually from many per¬ sons.
text_raw:
In  both  cases  the  capitalist  has  to  pay  out  money  constantly  to
many  persons,  and  to  receive  money  continually  from  many  per¬
sons.

text: This purely technical operation of disbursing and receiving money is in itself labour which, as long as the money serves as a means of payment, necessitates drawing up payment balances and acts of balancing accounts.
text_raw:
This  purely  technical  operation  of  disbursing  and  receiving
money  is  in  itself  labour  which,  as  long  as  the  money  serves  as
a  means  of  payment,  necessitates  drawing  up  payment  balances
and  acts  of  balancing  accounts.

text: This labour is a cost of circulation, i.e., not labour creating value.
text_raw:
This  labour  is  a  cost  of  circulation,
i.e.,  not  labour  creating  value.

text: It is shortened in being carried out by a special section of agents, or capitalists, for the rest of the capitalist class.
text_raw:
It  is  shortened  in  being  carried
out  by  a  special  section  of  agents,  or  capitalists,  for  the  rest  of  the
capitalist  class.

text: A definite portion of the capital must be on hand constantly as a hoard, as potential money-capital — a reserve of means of purchase, a reserve of means of payment, and idle capital in the form of money waiting to be put to work.
text_raw:
A  definite  portion  of  the  capital  must  be  on  hand  constantly
as  a  hoard,  as  potential  money-capital — a  reserve  of  means  of
purchase,  a  reserve  of  means  of  payment,  and  idle  capital  in
the  form  of  money  waiting  to  be  put  to  work.

text: Another portion streams back continually in this form.
text_raw:
Another  portion
streams  back  continually  in  this  form.

text: Aside from collecting, paying, and book-keeping, this entails safekeeping the hoard, which is an operation all in itself.
text_raw:
Aside  from  collecting,
paying,  and  book-keeping,  this  entails  safekeeping  the  hoard,
which  is  an  operation  all  in  itself.

text: It is, indeed, a continuous conversion of the hoard into means of circulation and means of payment, and its restoration by means of money secured through sales and from payments due.
text_raw:
It  is,  indeed,  a  continuous
conversion  of  the  hoard  into  means  of  circulation  and  means  of
payment,  and  its  restoration  by  means  of  money  secured  through
sales  and  from  payments  due.

text: This constant movement of the part of capital existing as money, dissociated from the function of capital itself, this purely technical function, causes its own labour and expense, classified as costs of circulation.
text_raw:
This  constant  movement  of  the  part
of  capital  existing  as  money,  dissociated  from  the  function  of
capital  itself,  this  purely  technical  function,  causes  its  own
labour  and  expense,  classified  as  costs  of  circulation.

text: The division of labour brings it about that these technical operations, dependent upon the functions of capital, should be performed for the entire capitalist class as much as possible by a special section of agents or capitalists as their exclusive function —
text_raw:
The  division  of  labour  brings  it  about  that  these  technical
operations,  dependent  upon  the  functions  of  capital,  should  be
performed  for  the  entire  capitalist  class  as  much  as  possible  by  a
special  section  of  agents  or  capitalists  as  their  exclusive  function —

text: or that these operations should be concentrated in their hands.
text_raw: or  that  these  operations  should  be  concentrated  in  their  hands.

text: We have here, as in merchant's capital, division of labour in a two-fold sense.
text_raw:
We  have  here,  as  in  merchant's  capital,  division  of  labour  in

text: It becomes a specialised business, and because performed as a specialised business for the money-mechanism of the whole class, it is concentrated and conducted on a large scale.

It  becomes  a  specialised  business,  and  because
performed  as  a  specialised  business  for  the  money-mechanism

text: A further division of labour takes place within it, both through division into various independent branches, and through segmentation of work within these branches (large offices, numerous book-keepers and cashiers, and far-reaching division of labour).
text_raw:
A  further  division  of  labour  takes  place  within  it,  both
through  division  into  various  independent  branches,  and  through
segmentation  of  work  within  these  branches  (large  offices,
numerous  book-keepers  and  cashiers,  and  far-reaching  division  of
labour).

text: Paying and receiving money, settling accounts, keeping current accounts, storing money, etc. — all this, dissociated from the acts necessitating these technical operations, makes money¬ dealing capital of the capital advanced for these functions.
text_raw:
Paying  and  receiving  money,  settling  accounts,  keeping
current  accounts,  storing  money,  etc. — all  this,  dissociated  from
the  acts  necessitating  these  technical  operations,  makes  money¬
dealing  capital  of  the  capital  advanced  for  these  functions.

text: The various operations, whose individualisation into specific businesses gives rise to the money trade, spring from the different purposes of money itself and from its functions, which capital in its money-form must therefore likewise carry out.
text_raw:
The  various  operations,  whose  individualisation  into  specific

in  its  money-form  must  therefore  likewise  carry  out.

text: In the Middle Ages, the merchant was merely one who, as Poppe rightly says, “transferred ” the goods produced by guilds or peas¬ ants.* The merchant becomes industrialist, or rather, makes crafts¬ men, particularly the small rural producers, work for him.

ants.*  The  merchant  becomes  industrialist,  or  rather,  makes  crafts¬

versely,  the  producer  becomes  merchant.

text: The master weaver, for instance, buys his wool or yarn himself and sells his cloth to the merchant, instead of receiving his wool from the merchant piecemeal and working for him together with his journeymen.

The  capitalist  then  appears  only

text: As a commodity the product must realise its value, must assume its transmuted form of money, in the process of circulation by its sale.
text_raw:
As  a  commodity  the  product  must  realise  its
value,  must  assume  its  transmuted  form  of  money,  in  the  process
of  circulation  by  its  sale.

text: It is also quite immaterial for this reason, whether this commodity is bought by a consumer as a necessity of life, or by a capitalist as means of production, i.e., as a com¬ ponent part of his capital.
text_raw:
It  is  also  quite  immaterial  for  this  reason,
whether  this  commodity  is  bought  by  a  consumer  as  a  necessity
of  life,  or  by  a  capitalist  as  means  of  production,  i.e.,  as  a  com¬
ponent  part  of  his  capital.

text: In the act of circulation commodity-ca¬ pital acts only as a commodity, not as a capital.
text_raw:
In  the  act  of  circulation  commodity-ca¬
pital  acts  only  as  a  commodity,  not  as  a  capital.

text: It is commodity- capital, as distinct from an ordinary commodity, 1) because it is weighted with surplus-value, the realisation of its value, therefore, being simultaneously the realisation of surplus-value; but this alters nothing about its simple existence as a commodity, as a product with a certain price;

2) because its function as a com¬ modity is a phase in its process of reproduction as capital, and therefore its movement as a commodity being only a partial move¬ ment of its process, is simultaneously its movement as capital.
text_raw:
2)  because  its  function  as  a  com¬
modity  is  a  phase  in  its  process  of  reproduction  as  capital,  and
therefore  its  movement  as  a  commodity  being  only  a  partial  move¬
ment  of  its  process,  is  simultaneously  its  movement  as  capital.

text: Yet it does not become that through the sale as such, but only through the connection of the sale with the whole movement of this specific quantity of value in the capacity of capital.
text_raw:
Yet  it  does  not  become  that  through  the  sale  as  such,  but  only
through  the  connection  of  the  sale  with  the  whole  movement  of
this  specific  quantity  of  value  in  the  capacity  of  capital.

text: In the same way as money-capital it really acts simply as money, i.e., as a means of buying commodities (the elements of pro¬ duction).
text_raw:
In  the  same  way  as  money-capital  it  really  acts  simply  as  money,
i.e.,  as  a  means  of  buying  commodities  (the  elements  of  pro¬
duction).

text: The fact that this money is simultaneously money- capital, a form of capital, does not emerge from the act of buying, the actual function which it here performs as money, but from the connection of this act with the total movement of capital, since this act, performed by capital as money, initiates the capitalist production process.'
text_raw:
The  fact  that  this  money  is  simultaneously  money-
capital,  a  form  of  capital,  does  not  emerge  from  the  act  of  buying,
the  actual  function  which  it  here  performs  as  money,  but  from
the  connection  of  this  act  with  the  total  movement  of  capital,
since  this  act,  performed  by  capital  as  money,  initiates  the
capitalist  production  process.'

text: But in so far as they actually function, i.e., actually play a role in the process, commodity-capital acts here only as a com¬ modity and money-capital only as money.
text_raw:
But  in  so  far  as  they  actually  function,  i.e.,  actually  play
a  role  in  the  process,  commodity-capital  acts  here  only  as  a  com¬
modity  and  money-capital  only  as  money.

text: At no time during the metamorphosis, viewed by itself, does the capitalist sell his com¬ modities as capital to the buyer, although to him they represent capital; nor does he give up money as capital to the seller.
text_raw:
At  no  time  during  the
metamorphosis,  viewed  by  itself,  does  the  capitalist  sell  his  com¬
modities  as  capital  to  the  buyer,  although  to  him  they  represent
capital;  nor  does  he  give  up  money  as  capital  to  the  seller.

text: In both cases he gives up his commodities simply as commodities, and money simply as money, i.e. , as a means of purchasing commodities.
text_raw:
In  both
cases  he  gives  up  his  commodities  simply  as  commodities,  and
money  simply  as  money,  i.e. ,  as  a  means  of  purchasing  commodities.

text: It is only in connection with the entire process, at the moment where the point of departure appears simultaneously as the point of return, in M — M' or C — C\ that capital in the process of circulation appears as capital (whereas in the process of production it appears as capital through the subordination of the

circulation  appears  as  capital  (whereas  in  the  process  of
production  it  appears  as  capital  through  the  subordination  of  the

text: What we have then is M', or M+AM, a sum of money equal to the sum originally advanced plus an increment — the realised surplus-value (regardless of whether the amount of value increased by AM exists in the form of money, or commodities, or elements of production).
text_raw:

sum  originally  advanced  plus  an  increment — the  realised

text: And it is precisely at this point of return where capital exists as realised capital, as an expanded value, that it never enters the circulation in this form — In so far as this point is fixed as a point of rest, whether real or imaginary — but rather appears to have been withdrawn from circulation as a result of the whole process.
text_raw:
And  it  is  precisely  at  this  point  of  return  where
capital  exists  as  realised  capital,  as  an  expanded  value,  that  it
never  enters  the  circulation  in  this  form — In  so  far  as  this  point

the  whole  process.

text: Whenever it is again expended, it is never given up to another as capital, but is sold to him as an ordinary com¬ modity, or given to him as ordinary money in exchange for commod¬ ities.

Whenever  it  is  again  expended,  it  is  never  given

modity,  or  given  to  him  as  ordinary  money  in  exchange  for  commod¬

text: It never appears as capital in its process of circulation, only as commodity or money, and at this point this is the only form of its existence for others.
text_raw:
It  never  appears  as  capital  in  its  process  of  circulation,  only
as  commodity  or  money,  and  at  this  point  this  is  the  only  form  of
its  existence  for  others.

text: Commodities and money are here capital not because commodities change into money, or money into com¬ modities, not in their actual relations to sellers or buyers, but only in their ideal relations to the capitalist himself (subjectively speaking), or as phases in the process of reproduction (objectively speaking).
text_raw:
Commodities  and  money  are  here  capital
not  because  commodities  change  into  money,  or  money  into  com¬
modities,  not  in  their  actual  relations  to  sellers  or  buyers,  but
only  in  their  ideal  relations  to  the  capitalist  himself  (subjectively
speaking),  or  as  phases  in  the  process  of  reproduction  (objectively
speaking).

text: Capital exists as capital in actual movement, not in the process of circulation, but only in the process of production, in the process by which labour-power is exploited.
text_raw:
Capital  exists  as  capital  in  actual  movement,  not  in
the  process  of  circulation,  but  only  in  the  process  of  production,
in  the  process  by  which  labour-power  is  exploited.

text: The matter is different with interest-bearing capital, how¬ ever, and it is precisely this difference which lends it its specific character.
text_raw:
The  matter  is  different  with  interest-bearing  capital,  how¬
ever,  and  it  is  precisely  this  difference  which  lends  it  its  specific
character.

text: The owner of money who desires to enhance his money as interest-bearing capital, turns it over to a third person, throws it into circulation, turns it into a commodity ds capital ; not just capital for himself, but also for others.
text_raw:
The  owner  of  money  who  desires  to  enhance  his  money
as  interest-bearing  capital,  turns  it  over  to  a  third  person,  throws
it  into  circulation,  turns  it  into  a  commodity  ds  capital ;  not  just
capital  for  himself,  but  also  for  others.

text: It is not capital merely for the man who gives it up, but is from the very first given to the third person as capital, as a value endowed with the use- value of creating surplus-value, of creating profit; a value which preserves itself in its movement and returns to its original owner, in this case the owner of money, after performing its function.
text_raw:
It  is  not  capital  merely
for  the  man  who  gives  it  up,  but  is  from  the  very  first  given  to
the  third  person  as  capital,  as  a  value  endowed  with  the  use-
value  of  creating  surplus-value,  of  creating  profit;  a  value  which
preserves  itself  in  its  movement  and  returns  to  its  original  owner,
in  this  case  the  owner  of  money,  after  performing  its  function.

text: Hence it leaves him only for a specified time, passes but tempo¬ rarily out of the possession of its owner into the possession of a func¬ tioning capitalist, is therefore neither given up in payment nor sold, but merely loaned, merely relinquished with the understand¬ ing that, first, it shall return to its point of departure after a definite time interval, and, second, that it shall return as realised capital--a capital having realised its use-value, its power of creating surplus-value.
text_raw:
Hence  it  leaves  him  only  for  a  specified  time,  passes  but  tempo¬
rarily  out  of  the  possession  of  its  owner  into  the  possession  of  a  func¬
tioning  capitalist,  is  therefore  neither  given  up  in  payment  nor
sold,  but  merely  loaned,  merely  relinquished  with  the  understand¬
ing  that,  first,  it  shall  return  to  its  point  of  departure  after  a
definite  time  interval,  and,  second,  that  it  shall  return  as  realised
capital--a  capital  having  realised  its  use-value,  its  power  of
creating  surplus-value.

text_raw: DIVISION  OF  PROFIT

text: Commodities loaned out as capital are loaned either as fixed or as circulating capital, depending on their properties.
text_raw:
Commodities  loaned  out  as  capital  are  loaned  either  as  fixed
or  as  circulating  capital,  depending  on  their  properties.

text: Money may be loaned out in either form.
text_raw:
Money
may  be  loaned  out  in  either  form.

text: It may be loaned as fixed cap<- ital, for instance, if it is paid back in the form of an annuity, whereby a portion of the capital flows back together with the in¬ terest.
text_raw:
It  may  be  loaned  as  fixed  cap<-
ital,  for  instance,  if  it  is  paid  back  in  the  form  of  an  annuity,
whereby  a  portion  of  the  capital  flows  back  together  with  the  in¬
terest.

text: Certain commodities, such as houses, ships, machines, etc., can be loaned out only as fixed capital by the nature of their use-values.
text_raw:
Certain  commodities,  such  as  houses,  ships,  machines,
etc.,  can  be  loaned  out  only  as  fixed  capital  by  the  nature  of  their
use-values.

text: Yet all loaned capital, whatever its form, and no matter how the nature of its use-value may modify its return, is always only a specific form of money-capital.
text_raw:
Yet  all  loaned  capital,  whatever  its  form,  and  no
matter  how  the  nature  of  its  use-value  may  modify  its  return,
is  always  only  a  specific  form  of  money-capital.

text: Because what is loaned out is always a definite sum of money, and it is this sum on which interest is calculated.
text_raw:
Because  what
is  loaned  out  is  always  a  definite  sum  of  money,  and  it  is  this
sum  on  which  interest  is  calculated.

text: Should whatever is loaned out be neither money nor circulating capital, it is also paid back in the way fixed capital returns.
text_raw:
Should  whatever  is  loaned
out  be  neither  money  nor  circulating  capital,  it  is  also  paid  back
in  the  way  fixed  capital  returns.

text: The lender periodically receives interest and a portion of the consumed value of the fixed capital itself, this being an equivalent for the periodic wear and tear.
text_raw:
The  lender  periodically  receives
interest  and  a  portion  of  the  consumed  value  of  the  fixed  capital
itself,  this  being  an  equivalent  for  the  periodic  wear  and  tear.

text: And at the end of the stipulated term the unconsumed portion of the loaned fixed capital is returned in kind.
text_raw:
And  at  the  end  of  the  stipulated  term  the  unconsumed  portion
of  the  loaned  fixed  capital  is  returned  in  kind.

text: If the loaned capital is circulating capital, it is likewise returned in the manner peculiar to circulating capital.
text_raw:
If  the  loaned
capital  is  circulating  capital,  it  is  likewise  returned  in  the
manner  peculiar  to  circulating  capital.

text: The manner of reflux is, therefore, always determined by the actual circuit described by capital in the act of reproduction and by its specific varieties.
text_raw:
The  manner  of  reflux  is,  therefore,  always  determined  by  the
actual  circuit  described  by  capital  in  the  act  of  reproduction  and  by
its  specific  varieties.

text: But as for loaned capital, its reflux assumes the form of return payments, because its advance, by which it is transferred, possesses the form of a loan.
text_raw:
But  as  for  loaned  capital,  its  reflux  assumes
the  form  of  return  payments,  because  its  advance,  by  which  it  is
transferred,  possesses  the  form  of  a  loan.

text: In this chapter we treat only of actual money-capital, from which the other forms of loaned capital are derived.
text_raw:
In  this  chapter  we  treat  only  of  actual  money-capital,  from
which  the  other  forms  of  loaned  capital  are  derived.

text: The loaned capital flows back in two ways.
text_raw: The  loaned  capital  flows  back  in  two  ways.

text: In the process of reproduction it returns to the functioning capitalist, and then its return repeats itself once more as transfer to the lender, the money-capitalist, as return payment to the real owner, its legal point of departure.
text_raw:
In  the  process  of
reproduction  it  returns  to  the  functioning  capitalist,  and  then
its  return  repeats  itself  once  more  as  transfer  to  the  lender,  the
money-capitalist,  as  return  payment  to  the  real  owner,  its  legal
point  of  departure.

text: In the actual process of circulation, capital appears always as a commodity or as money, and its movement always is broken up into a series of purchases and sales.
text_raw:
In  the  actual  process  of  circulation,  capital  appears  always
as  a  commodity  or  as  money,  and  its  movement  always  is  broken
up  into  a  series  of  purchases  and  sales.

text: In short, the process of cir¬ culation resolves itself into the metamorphosis of commodities.
text_raw:
In  short,  the  process  of  cir¬
culation  resolves  itself  into  the  metamorphosis  of  commodities.

text: It is different, when we consider the process of reproduction as a whole.
text_raw:
It  is  different,  when  we  consider  the  process  of  reproduction  as
a  whole.

sum  of  money  is  expended  and  returns  after  a  certain  period  with
an  increment.

The  advanced  sum  of  money  returns  together  with
a  surplus-value.

text_raw:
But  now,  being  loaned  out  as  capital,  money  is

text: This relation to itself, in which capital presents itself when the capitalist production process is viewed as a whole and as a single unity, and in which capital appears as money that begets money, is here imparted to it as its character, its designation, without any intermediary move¬ ment.
text_raw:
This  relation  to  itself,  in
which  capital  presents  itself  when  the  capitalist  production
process  is  viewed  as  a  whole  and  as  a  single  unity,  and  in  which
capital  appears  as  money  that  begets  money,  is  here  imparted  to  it
as  its  character,  its  designation,  without  any  intermediary  move¬
ment.

text: And it is relinquished with this designation when loaned out as money-capital.
text_raw:

text: The money is first converted into means of production; production transforms them into commodities; through, sale of the commodities they aro reconverted into money and return in this form into the hands of the capitalist who had originally advanced the capital in the form of money.
text_raw:
The  money  is  first  converted  into  means
of  production;  production  transforms  them  into  commodities;
through,  sale  of  the  commodities  they  aro  reconverted  into  money
and  return  in  this  form  into  the  hands  of  the  capitalist  who  had
originally  advanced  the  capital  in  the  form  of  money.

text: But in the case of interest-bearing capital, the return, like alienation, is the result of a legal transaction between the owner of the capi¬ tal and a second party.
text_raw:
But  in  the
case  of  interest-bearing  capital,  the  return,  like  alienation,  is
the  result  of  a  legal  transaction  between  the  owner  of  the  capi¬
tal  and  a  second  party.

text: We see only the alienation and the return payment.
text_raw:
We  see  only  the  alienation  and  the  return
payment.

text_raw: Whatever  passes  in  the  interim  is  obliterated.

text: But since money advanced as capital has the property of re¬ turning to the person who advanced it, to the one who expended it as capital, and since M — G — M' is the immanent form of the movement of capital, the owner of the money can, for this very reason, loan it out as capital, as something that has the property of returning to its point of departure, of preserving, and increasing, its value in the course of its movement.
text_raw:
But  since  money  advanced  as  capital  has  the  property  of  re¬
turning  to  the  person  who  advanced  it,  to  the  one  who  expended
it  as  capital,  and  since  M — G — M'  is  the  immanent  form  of  the
movement  of  capital,  the  owner  of  the  money  can,  for  this  very
reason,  loan  it  out  as  capital,  as  something  that  has  the  property  of
returning  to  its  point  of  departure,  of  preserving,  and  increasing,
its  value  in  the  course  of  its  movement.

text: He gives it away as capital, because it returns to its point of departure after having been employed as capital, hence can be restored by the borrower after a certain period precisely because it has come back to him.
text_raw:
He  gives  it  away  as
capital,  because  it  returns  to  its  point  of  departure  after  having  been
employed  as  capital,  hence  can  be  restored  by  the  borrower  after
a  certain  period  precisely  because  it  has  come  back  to  him.

text: Loaning money as capital — its alienation on the condition of it being returned after a certain time — presupposes, therefore, that it will be actually employed as capital, and that it actually flows back to its starting-point.
text_raw:
Loaning  money  as  capital — its  alienation  on  the  condition
of  it  being  returned  after  a  certain  time — presupposes,  therefore,
that  it  will  be  actually  employed  as  capital,  and  that  it  actually
flows  back  to  its  starting-point.

text: The real cycle made by money as capital is, therefore, the premise for the legal transaction by which the borrower must return the money to the lender.
text_raw:
The  real  cycle  made  by  money
as  capital  is,  therefore,  the  premise  for  the  legal  transaction  by
which  the  borrower  must  return  the  money  to  the  lender.

text_raw:
If  the
borrower  does  not  use  the  money  as  capital,  that  is  his  own  busi¬
ness.

text: The lender loans it as capital, and as such it is supposed to perform the functions of capital, which include the circuit of money-capital until it returns to its starting-point in the form of money.
text_raw:
The  lender  loans  it  as  capital,  and  as  such  it  is  supposed
to  perform  the  functions  of  capital,  which  include  the  circuit
of  money-capital  until  it  returns  to  its  starting-point  in  the  form
of  money.

text: The acts of circulation, M — C and C — M', in which a certain amount of value functions as money or commodities, are but intermediate processes, mere phases of the total movement.

The  acts  of  circulation,  M — C  and  C — M',  in  which  a  certain
amount  of  value  functions  as  money  or  commodities,  are  but
intermediate  processes,  mere  phases  of  the  total  movement.

text: As capital, it performs the entire movement M — M'.
text_raw:
As
capital,  it  performs  the  entire  movement  M — M'.

text_raw:
It  is  advanced
as  money  or  a  sum  of  values  in  one  form  or  another,  and  returns
as  a  sum  of  values.

purchasing  commodities,  or,  if  this  sum  of  values  is  in  commod¬
ity-form,  does  not  sell  it  for  money.

He  advances  it  as  capital,
as  M — M’,  as  a  value,  which  returns  to  its  point  of  departure  after
a  certain  term.

text_raw: He  lends  instead  of  buying  or  selling.

text: This lending, therefore, is the appropriate form of alienating value as capital, instead of alienating it as money or commodities.
text_raw:
This  lending,
therefore,  is  the  appropriate  form  of  alienating  value  as  capital,
instead  of  alienating  it  as  money  or  commodities.

actions  which  have  nothing  to  do  with  the  capitalist  process

We  have  so  far  only  considered  the  movements  of  loaned  capital
betweeh  its  owner  and  the  industrial  capitalist.

text_raw:
Now  we  must
inquire  into  interest.

text: The lender expends his money as capital; the amount of value, which he relinquishes to another, is capital, and consequently returns to him.
text_raw:
The  lender  expends  his  money  as  capital;  the  amount  of  value,
which  he  relinquishes  to  another,  is  capital,  and  consequently

text: But the mere return of it would not be the reflux of the loaned sum of value as capital , but merely the return of a loaned sum of value.

But  the  mere  return  of  it  would  not  be  the  reflux
of  the  loaned  sum  of  value  as  capital ,  but  merely  the  return  of  a
loaned  sum  of  value.

text: To return as capital, the advanced sum of value must not only be preserved in the movement but must also expand, must increase in value, i. e., must return with a surplils- value, as M+ AM, the latter being interest or a portion of the aver¬ age profit, which does not remain in the hands of the operating capitalist, but falls to the share of the money-capitalist.

To  return  as  capital,  the  advanced  sum  of
value  must  not  only  be  preserved  in  the  movement  but  must  also

age  profit,  which  does  not  remain  in  the  hands  of  the  operating
capitalist,  but  falls  to  the  share  of  the  money-capitalist.

The  fact  that  the  latter  has  relinquished  it  as  capital  implies

text: What is alienated in an ordinary sale?
text_raw: What  is  alienated  in  an  ordinary  sale?

text: Not the value of the sold commodity, for this merely changes its form.
text_raw:
Not  the  value  of  the  sold
commodity,  for  this  merely  changes  its  form.

text: The value exists ideally in a commodity as its price before it actually passes as money into the hands of the seller.
text_raw:
The  value  exists
ideally  in  a  commodity  as  its  price  before  it  actually  passes  as
money  into  the  hands  of  the  seller.

text: The same value and the same amount of value merely change their form.
text_raw:
The  same  value  and  the  same
amount  of  value  merely  change  their  form.

text_raw:
In  the  one  instance
they  exist  in  commodity-form,  in  the  other  in  the  form  of  money.

text: What is really alienated by the seller, and, therefore, passes into the individual or productive consumption of the buyer, is the use- value of the commodity — the commodity as a use-value.
text_raw:
What  is  really  alienated  by  the  seller,  and,  therefore,  passes  into
the  individual  or  productive  consumption  of  the  buyer,  is  the  use-
value  of  the  commodity — the  commodity  as  a  use-value.

text: What, now, is the use-value which the money-capitalist gives up for the period of the loan and relinquishes to the productive capitalist — the borrower?
text_raw:
What,  now,  is  the  use-value  which  the  money-capitalist  gives
up  for  the  period  of  the  loan  and  relinquishes  to  the  productive
capitalist — the  borrower?

text: It is the use-value which the money acquires by being capable of becoming capital, of performing the functions of capital, and creating a definite surplus-value, the aver¬ age profit (whatever is above or below it appears here as a mere accident) during its process, besides preserving its original mag¬ nitude of value.
text_raw:
It  is  the  use-value  which  the  money
acquires  by  being  capable  of  becoming  capital,  of  performing  the
functions  of  capital,  and  creating  a  definite  surplus-value,  the  aver¬
age  profit  (whatever  is  above  or  below  it  appears  here  as  a  mere
accident)  during  its  process,  besides  preserving  its  original  mag¬
nitude  of  value.

text: In the case of the other commodities the use-value is ultimately consumed.
text_raw:
In  the  case  of  the  other  commodities  the  use-value
is  ultimately  consumed.

text: Their substance disappears, and with it their value.
text_raw:
Their  substance  disappears,  and  with  it
their  value.

text: In contrast, the commodity-capital is peculiar in that its value and use-value not only remain intact but also increase, through consumption of its use-value.
text_raw:
In  contrast,  the  commodity-capital  is  peculiar  in  that
its  value  and  use-value  not  only  remain  intact  but  also  increase,
through  consumption  of  its  use-value.

text: It is this use-value of money as capital — this faculty of produc¬ ing an average profit — which the money-capitalist relinquishes to the industrial capitalist for the period, during which he places the loaned capital at the latter’s disposal.
text_raw:
It  is  this  use-value  of  money  as  capital — this  faculty  of  produc¬
ing  an  average  profit — which  the  money-capitalist  relinquishes
to  the  industrial  capitalist  for  the  period,  during  which  he  places
the  loaned  capital  at  the  latter’s  disposal.

text: Money thus loaned has in this respect a certain similarity with labour-power in its relation to the industrial capitalist.
text_raw:
Money  thus  loaned  has  in  this  respect  a  certain  similarity  with
labour-power  in  its  relation  to  the  industrial  capitalist.

text: With the difference that the latter pays for the value of labour-power, where¬ as he simply pays back the value of the loaned capital.
text_raw:
With  the
difference  that  the  latter  pays  for  the  value  of  labour-power,  where¬
as  he  simply  pays  back  the  value  of  the  loaned  capital.

text: The use- value of labour-power for the industrial capitalist is that labour- power creates more value (profit) in its consumption than it pos¬ sesses itself, and than it costs.
text_raw:
The  use-
value  of  labour-power  for  the  industrial  capitalist  is  that  labour-
power  creates  more  value  (profit)  in  its  consumption  than  it  pos¬
sesses  itself,  and  than  it  costs.

text: This additional value is use-value for the industrial capitalist.
text_raw:
This  additional  value  is  use-value
for  the  industrial  capitalist.

text_raw:
And  in  like  manner  the  use-value  of
loaned  capital  appears  as  its  faculty  of  begetting  and  increasing
value.

text: The money-capitalist, in fact, alienates a use-value, and thus whatever he gives away is given as a commodity.

The  money-capitalist,  in  fact,  alienates  a  use-value,  and  thus
whatever  he  gives  away  is  given  as  a  commodity.

It  is  to  this  ex¬
tent  that  the  analogy  with  a  commodity  per  se  is  complete.

text: Because, 1) money may be converted into elements of production and is, as is, merely an abstract expression of them — their existence as value;

2) the material elements of wealth have the property of potentially becoming capital, because their supplementary opposite, which makes them into capital, namely wage-labour, is available on the basis of capitalist produc¬ tion.

2)  the  material  elements  of  wealth
have  the  property  of  potentially  becoming  capital,  because

text: The contradictory social features of material wealth— its antagonism to labour as wage-labour — are expressed in capitalist property as such independently of the production process.
